updated_claim: Japan's FIT/FIP for biomass power pays ¥24/kWh (~$160/MWh at ¥150/$) for projects using imported general woody biomass (wood pellets, PKS, palm trunk) with capacity under 10 MW — a rate that has held steady through FY2025-26. Large-scale projects (≥10 MW) do not receive a fixed ¥24/kWh; they are subject to competitive FIP tender, with an upper-bid ceiling of ¥14/kWh in FY2024 (and have drawn no bids since 2021-22). METI has signalled intent to discontinue FIT/FIP support for new large-scale woody biomass (≥10 MW) from FY2026. The ¥24/kWh rate for sub-10 MW projects is the mechanism that sustains a Japanese buyer willingness-to-pay of $140–160/t for SEA wood pellets and PKS, versus SEA domestic industrial buyers at $80–100/t — but this arbitrage applies to the sub-10 MW segment; large-scale plants are on contracted or tender-derived rates which may be materially lower.

Japan's trade and industry ministry (METI) has decided to maintain the feed-in-premium (FiP) and feed-in-tariff (FiT) price for small biomass power projects at ¥24/kWh ($160/MWh) for the April 2025–March 2026 fiscal year. Applies to general woody and agricultural biomass with less than 10MW capacity. For 10MW+ plants: competitive tender system.

large_scale_10MW_plus.status: No bids submitted since FY2021-22; METI planning to discontinue for new projects from FY2026
large_scale_10MW_plus.note: Most of Japan's large biomass plants (100+ MW co-firing and dedicated plants) were contracted under earlier fixed-rate FIT vintages from 2012–2017 at 21–24 yen/kWh, which they retain for their 20-year term

rate_structure_clarification.vintage_note: Plants approved 2012–2016 received 24 yen/kWh for general biomass regardless of size; rate for large new-entrant plants was cut to 21 yen/kWh from FY2017, then moved to competitive tender from FY2018-19

claim_accuracy_assessment: The original claim's ¥24/kWh figure is accurate for (a) small-scale sub-10 MW projects currently, and (b) legacy large-scale plants contracted 2012–2016 that retain their original FIT rate. It is NOT the current rate for new large-scale projects. The price-wedge logic (Japanese buyers paying $140–160/t vs SEA domestic $80–100/t) is directionally correct for sub-10 MW plants and legacy contracts, but overstated if applied uniformly to all current Japanese biomass power buyers.
